Consult Summary:
- Postpartum patient with recent cesarean section presenting with acute shortness of breath and a cough, with concern for postpartum thromboembolism; advised urgent hospital evaluation; patient elected to go to the hospital herself with baby.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden onset shortness of breath within the last hour, occurring at rest while watching TV; associated with chest soreness on deep inspiration and tenderness of the C-section scar. Cough began yesterday.
- Timeline:
  - C-section performed 4 weeks ago.
  - Cough started yesterday.
  - Shortness of breath started about 1 hour prior to evaluation.
  - Patient notes feeling heart rate may be faster than usual and increased stress.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: None described beyond breaching stress and SOB; no explicit relief.
- Associated symptoms: Cough; chest soreness on deep breath; scar tenderness. No chest pain reported.
- Other relevant history: Postpartum period after recent C-section; baby is present and well; no fever or flu symptoms reported recently.
- ROS notes: No other medical problems reported. Patient reports regular use of codeine since the C-section but not in the past week. Allergic to ibuprofen.
- Medical history: No prior medical problems mentioned other than recent C-section.
- Medications: Codeine (taken regularly after C-section; dose/frequency not documented; last week not taken). Ibuprofen allergy noted.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen.

Past Medical History:
- Recent cesarean section (4 weeks ago).
- No other chronic medical conditions documented.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen.

Medications:
- Codeine (taken regularly after C-section; dose/route/frequency not documented; last taken about a week ago).
- Allergy to Ibuprofen (reaction not specified).

Social History:
- With baby at home; partner at work and not present at the moment.
- No other social history details provided (e.g., smoking, alcohol, substance use).

Family History:
- Not mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: Patient reports SOB and tachycardia; chest feels sore with deep inspiration; C-section scar tender.
- Cardiac/respiratory exam: No formal findings beyond subjective tachycardia and chest/scar tenderness described. No chest pain reported.

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results provided in the transcript.
- Clinician suggested potential hospital evaluation (imaging/assessment to assess for thromboembolism) but no tests ordered here.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Shortness of breath in the postpartum period with recent cesarean section.
  - Assessment: Concern for postpartum thromboembolism (DVT/PE) given acute SOB after recent C-section.
  - Plan:
    - Recommend urgent hospital evaluation for further assessment (possible imaging and labs to evaluate for clots).
    - Patient advised to go to the hospital; option to call an ambulance; patient chose to self-transport with baby.
    - Do not take Codeine during this period.
    - Bring baby and essentials; proceed quickly.
    - At hospital, if a clot is found, treatment with anticoagulation may be given (per clinician’s explanation).
    - Reassurance provided that clots are possible but require evaluation.
- Issue 2: Tachycardia suspected in context of SOB and pain.
  - Assessment: Heart rate described as slightly fast by clinician.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor and evaluate at the hospital; no outpatient-specific treatment detailed beyond hospital evaluation.
- Issue 3: Medication and allergy considerations.
  - Assessment: Ibuprofen allergy documented.
  - Plan:
    - Note allergy; avoid ibuprofen as clinically appropriate during ongoing evaluation (no specific instruction given in transcript beyond allergy documentation).

General Plan:
- Proceed to urgent hospital evaluation for SOB postpartum evaluation of possible thromboembolism.
- Avoid Codeine temporarily until evaluated.
- Provide support for taking baby to hospital; ensure quick disposition.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Exact vital signs (BP, HR numeric, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation) are not provided.
  - No imaging or laboratory results available.
  - No discharge instructions or follow-up appointment details.
  - No reconciliation of other medications or comprehensive ROS beyond SOB and cough.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Date of birth provided as two conflicting values: “April 20, 1980” (implied by “nineteen eighty”) and “nineteen eighty three.” Conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; minor inconsistencies in DOB. No significant audio issues noted.
